sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Capella University and Southern New Hampshire University (Capella vs SNHU) differ primarily in ownership, enrollment, tuition, and location. Capella University is a private for-profit institution based in Minneapolis, with an undergraduate enrollment of 18,364 students. In contrast, Southern New Hampshire University is a private nonprofit institution located in Manchester, with an undergraduate enrollment of 163,164 students. Tuition for in-state students at Capella is $14,400, while Southern New Hampshire University charges $17,200. These distinctions highlight differences in institutional structure, scale, cost, and geographic setting between Capella and SNHU.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing cost, Capella University and Southern New Hampshire University (Capella vs SNHU) show notable differences. Capella charges $14,400 for both in-state and out-of-state tuition, whereas Southern New Hampshire University has a higher tuition rate of $17,200 for both categories. Additionally, the median debt for students who complete their programs at Capella is $14,968, which is lower than Southern New Hampshire University's median debt of $21,082. These figures indicate that Capella may offer a more affordable option in terms of tuition and student debt burden compared to Southern New Hampshire University.

This contrast in enrollment and setting reflects differing scales and approaches within their respective educational frameworks, illustrating key distinctions when considering Capella vs SNHU.
